messages:
alex chen: Heads up — NE cluster showing sustained request queueing for /generate. p50 latency fine, but p95 jumped from ~320ms to 1.8s in the last 20m. GPU pod Pending count = 42 (was 3). Network retransmits and proxy egress errors in the logs. Anyone seeing this elsewhere?

mike ramos: seeing same signal. looks like front proxies hitting connection waits to storage region-us-east1-s3. some pods stuck in Terminating -> Pending loop. suspecting node pressure + network path flapping.

sana patel: paging metrics — traffic spike tied to retail partner campaign (go-live in 3h). projected QPS for NE is +75% from baseline for next 12h. pre-run forecast suggests we’ll need ~280 extra A100 GPU-hours/day if we keep current model sizes and batching.

li wang: quick check — autoscaler config has max=120 pods for model-service-ne. current desired=95, available=53. scaling events are being rate-limited by kube-controller because of scheduling failures (taints + resource fragmentation).

emily: cost note — on-demand A100 avg $2.75/hr -> 280 GPU-hrs/day ~= $770/day extra; if this persists 3 days ≈ $2.3k. reserved-burst (our dedicated pool) would cut to ~35% of that delta. but need to balance latency SLOs.

alex chen: mike, can you post the failing scheduler logs + the proxy error snippet? also ops-bot, can you run a quick simulation of cross-region burst to see if we can safely route 20% to eu-west for next 6h?

mike ramos: pasted logs: \n```\nI0320 15:34:21.123 kube-scheduler: failed to schedule pod model-service-ne-ccf due to insufficient nvidia.com/gpu on nodes (fragmented), 14 pending\nW0320 15:34:45 proxy: upstream write failed: connection reset by peer -> region-us-east1-s3, retries=6\n```\n
mike ramos: also tried node drain -> new pods hang in Pending due to kubelet image pull limits hitting per-node bandwidth cap.

ops-bot: cross-region-burst-sim: success. routing 20% traffic -> eu-west reduces NE GPU load by ~18% but increases median tail latency by ~80ms due to network RTT. No capacity alarms triggered in EU.

sana patel: proposal: 1) pre-stage quantized model variants to edge racks in NE (reduce per-token GPU work ~1.9x), 2) spin up 40 GPUs from dedicated burst pool for 8h, 3) enable region fallback for non-SLA customers. Thoughts?

li wang: +1 on pre-stage. we need a short terraform change to increase dedicated pool and a kube-scheduler tweak to prefer packing. snippet: \n```hcl\nresource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "ne_burst" {\n  region = "us-east1-ne"\n  gpu_count = 40\n  duration_hours = 8\n}\n```\nalso set schedulerPolicy: { "preference": "binpack" } in nodegroup to reduce fragmentation.

emily: cost estimate for that plan: 40 GPUs * 8h * $2.2/hr (reserved-burst rate) ≈ $704. Quantization rollout risk: small drop in Rouge/QA for some prompts — need quick eval on 100 canonical prompts.

alex chen: ok action list: @mike deploy kernel of schedulerPolicy change + monitor for 15m, @li create terraform change to claim 40 GPUs from dedicated burst, @sana run eval with 100 prompts against quantized model and post delta, @emily confirm finance ok with $1k ad-hoc spend. If fallback to EU is used, enable region routing flag and throttle non-SLA customers by 30%.

mike ramos: started scheduler change now. command: \n```bash\nkubectl apply -f scheduler-policy-preference.yaml && kubectl get events --watch \n```\nwill report back in 10.

sana patel: running eval now. quick preview: avg quality drop ~2.1% BLEU-ish proxy for our metrics on the set, tail worst-case 6%. posting results in 12m.

emily: finance approved up to $1.5k emergency pool spend. approved. :white_check_mark:

li wang: submitted terraform PR -> #4872. includes pool claim + label for binpack nodes. requesting review from infra-ops.

mike ramos: scheduler change applied. after 7m Pending GPUs dropped from 42 -> 9 and p95 latency down to 620ms. still seeing a handful of proxy resets — tracing to an overloaded NAT gateway on one subnet.

alex chen: great improvement. next: spin up burst GPUs + fix NAT path. @ops-bot can you queue a NAT gateway scale for subnet-a-ne and keep a rollback window?

ops-bot: nat-gateway-scale: scheduled scale-up for subnet-a-ne -> +2 NAT gateways at 16:40 UTC, rollback window 18:40 UTC. monitoring enabled.

sana patel: eval done — quantized model delta: mean metric -2.3%, p95 worse by 4% for our safety prompts. recommended: use quantized for non-critical routes first and A/B traffic 10/90.

alex chen: decision: roll quantized to 10% non-SLA immediately, spin dedicated 40 GPUs for 8h, enable region fallback at 20% if we see NE load >85% capacity. mike, li — coordinate the rollout. I'll update incident channel if anything regresses. thanks all. :rocket:
